title: Support and training for students with special educational needs in schools
asked: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis asked whether the Ministry provides guidelines to teachers and schools on handling children with special educational needs (SEN), how many hours of SEN training teachers receive annually, and whether the Ministry conducts an annual review of best practices across schools.
response: The Ministry provides guidelines, information and video resources to schools to support students with SEN. All new teachers undergo basic SEN training in pre-service, and in-service teachers deepen their skills through workshops, Networked Learning Communities and Micro-Learning Units. Each school has Teachers Trained in Special Needs who completed a 130-hour NIE certificate, and mainstream schools have SEN Officers who develop customised interventions. MOE shares best practices among mainstream and Special Education schools and continually reviews its guidelines and good practices.

key_points.point: MOE provides guidelines, information and video resources to schools to support students with SEN.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The Ministry provides guidelines, information and video resources to schools to support students with special educational needs (SEN).

key_points.point: All new teachers undergo basic training covering how to engage students with SEN during pre-service training.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: All new teachers undergo basic training covering how to engage students with SEN during their pre-service training.

key_points.point: In-service teachers deepen SEN-related skills through workshops and Networked Learning Communities in inclusive pedagogy.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: they continue to deepen their SEN-related skills through workshops and Networked Learning Communities in areas, such as inclusive pedagogy.

key_points.point: Each school has Teachers Trained in Special Needs who completed a 130-hour certificate-level course by NIE.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Each school also has Teachers Trained in Special Needs who have completed a 130-hour certificate-level course conducted by the National Institute of Education.

key_points.point: All mainstream schools have SEN Officers who develop customised interventions for students with SEN, particularly those with higher needs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: All mainstream schools also have SEN Officers who work with school personnel to develop customised interventions to support the specific needs of students with SEN, particularly those with higher needs.

key_points.point: MOE facilitates systematic sharing of best practices among mainstream schools and between mainstream and Special Education schools.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Education (MOE) facilitates systematic sharing of best practices among mainstream schools, as well as between mainstream schools and Special Education schools.

key_points.point: SEN Resource Portal offers schools structures, guidelines and resources to support students with SEN.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: we have the SEN Resource Portal and this offers schools with the structures, the guidelines and the resources to support students with SEN.

key_points.point: SEN:se Online Professional Development on OPAL 2.0 covers perceptions about SEN, support principles on needs not diagnosis, and strategies for positive classroom culture and behavioural support.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: we also have the SEN:se Online Professional Development, a series of practice oriented online modules on OPAL 2.0 for teachers' just-in-time learning and also bite-sized, locally produced modules covering perceptions about SEN, support principles on needs and not on diagnosis, as well as strategies on positive classroom culture and behavioural support.

key_points.point: Separate information is pushed to parents through Parents Gateway to help them support children with SEN.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: As to the Member's question about parents, there is separate information that we push through our Parents Gateway, to our parents, to be able to allow them to in turn, look towards supporting their children with SEN where the needs apply.

key_points.point: The exact number of SEN training hours was not stated; teachers have flexibility to choose lessons and modules.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: In terms of the specific number of hours in terms of SEN, I do not have the exact number of hours that we have for our teachers, but suffice to say, they have the flexibility to look at what lessons they require, what additional modules they wish to be able to have; and they can apply that in turn, because it is readily accessible for them.

left_open: The exact annual number of hours of SEN training provided to teachers.
Whether the review of best practices across schools is conducted annually.
Whether the guide is made available to parents as well as teachers.
Whether there are specified minimum hours for SEN-related continuous professional development.
supplementary: Supplementary questions asked about consistency and parent access to SEN guidelines, and the number of SEN training hours and whether minimum hours are required.
